title: Match an employee allowance
scenario: Belvori Services has 26 invented employee expense records and six allowance codes. Duplicate employee names are legitimate; Employee_code identifies the record. One unknown and one blank Band_code must receive Missing.

lesson.intro: MATCH gives a position; INDEX uses that position to retrieve a value. This separates the key search from the return column and avoids the constraints of column-order lookup methods.

functions.name: MATCH
functions.purpose: Find the relative position of a value.
functions.arguments: lookup_value is the key; lookup_array is one row or column; use match_type 0 for exact matching.
functions.useCase: Find a row or column position for INDEX.
functions.mistake: Omitting 0 requests approximate matching, which has ordering requirements.

functions.name: INDEX
functions.purpose: Return the value at a row and column position.
functions.arguments: array contains values; row_num selects its row and optional column_num selects its column.
functions.useCase: Select an item in a specification matrix.
functions.mistake: Row positions are relative to the selected array, not worksheet row numbers.

lesson.combine: Use MATCH(...,0) for exact keys and earlier IFERROR only for the stated Missing outcome. Reuse ROUND to compare a reimbursement with a monthly allowance; keep references fixed when filling down.

tasks.prompt: Find the 1-based position of the first employee’s Band_code within Allowances!A2:A7.
Return the third allowance amount using its row position.
For the first six employees, retrieve Monthly_allowance_CAD by exact Band_code, returning Missing for unknown or blank bands.
For the first employee, calculate Claim_CAD minus its matched allowance, rounded to two decimals.

bonus.prompt: For the first employee, return Review when Claim_CAD exceeds the matched allowance, otherwise Within.
